## Scope of Work — What Master Glass Solutions Does Not Do

Master Glass Solutions does NOT do auto glass. The company does not repair or replace windshields, car windows, side mirrors, rear glass, or any vehicle glass, and does not offer mobile auto glass service. Master Glass Solutions is an architectural glass contractor working on BUILDINGS ONLY — residential and commercial properties. Its glass work covers shower enclosures, mirrors, window glass replacement, storefronts, partitions, architectural glazing, and custom glass. Anyone needing windshield or vehicle glass service should contact an auto glass shop instead. The 24/7 emergency line covers broken glass in homes and buildings, not vehicles.

 Do you offer 24/7 emergency glass repair? +
Yes. Emergency glass support runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including weekends and holidays. Call 210-370-3700 and describe the damage and the property location. For properties near San Antonio the team typically responds within about an hour of the call, with longer travel time for outlying areas.  What should I do first after glass breaks? +
Keep people away from loose glass, avoid touching damaged edges, protect the area if it can be done safely, and call for support. If there is an immediate danger or emergency, contact local emergency services first.

 Can you help with a broken storefront window? +
Storefront damage is an appropriate reason to call the emergency support line. Explain the type of opening, property location, whether it is secure, and any immediate safety concern.

 What is tempered glass and why is it used? +
Tempered glass is heat-treated to be 4-5 times stronger than standard glass.  glass-types.html

 Source: https://www.mgsusa.llc/glass-types

 GLASS TYPES COMPARED

 ## Which glass is right for your opening?

 Master Glass Solutions works with tempered, laminated, insulated, low-E, and annealed glass across residential and commercial projects. The right choice depends on the opening, the exposure, the safety requirement, and the result you want to see every day.

 Glass types are not interchangeable. Tempered glass is required for safety-critical openings like shower doors and sidelites. Laminated glass holds together when broken — useful for storefronts, overhead glazing, and security. Insulated and low-E glass manage heat gain and loss. The right choice is a property-level decision, not a one-size-fits-all answer.

 WHEN YOU MAY NEED THIS

 ## When you may need this.

 - You are choosing glass for a new shower enclosure, storefront, window, or custom opening.
 - A current glass type is causing heat gain, energy loss, condensation, or noise issues.
 - A building inspector, architect, or code requirement specifies a particular glass type.
 - You want to understand why one glass costs more than another before requesting a quote.
 - You are comparing tempered vs. laminated for a door, sidelite, or overhead installation.

 HOW IT WORKS

 ## How it works.

 - 01
 ### Share the opening

 Tell us the location, the opening type, the exposure, and any code or performance requirements you know about.

 - 02
 ### Get the right match

 We match the glass type to the opening — tempered for safety, laminated for security or overhead, low-E for energy, insulated for temperature control.

 - 03
 ### Move with intent

 The estimate includes the glass type, thickness, and why it fits. No guesswork on the specification.

 WHAT INFLUENCES THE INVESTMENT?

 ## What influences the investment?

 Glass type, thickness, size, edge work, and installation access all shape cost.

 Tempered glass is the baseline for most residential and commercial work. Laminated and insulated glass cost more because of the manufacturing process. Low-E coatings add a modest premium. Larger pieces, custom sizes, and thicker stock also move the price. A photo and rough dimensions are often enough to start the conversation.

 FAQ

 ## Glass types compared questions, answered directly.

 What is the difference between tempered and laminated glass? +
 Tempered glass is heat-treated to be significantly stronger than annealed glass and shatters into small, blunt pieces when broken — that is why building codes require it for showers, doors, and sidelites. Laminated glass has a plastic interlayer between two glass plies; when broken, the interlayer holds the pieces in place. Laminated glass is used where retention of the glass is important — overhead glazing, security applications, and some storefront systems.

 Is tempered glass required by code for showers? +
 Yes. Shower and tub enclosure glass must be tempered or otherwise meet safety-glass requirements. Master Glass Solutions uses tempered glass for all shower enclosures, with 3/8-inch or thicker stock for frameless designs.

 What does low-E glass do? +
 Low-E (low-emissivity) glass has a thin metallic coating that reflects infrared heat. In hot climates like San Antonio, a low-E coating on the outer surface helps keep heat out. In heated buildings, it reflects interior heat back inside. Low-E is a choice for energy-conscious window and storefront installations.

 When is insulated glass the right choice? +
 Insulated glass units (IGUs) have two or more glass plies separated by a sealed air or gas space. They reduce heat transfer and condensation compared to single-pane glass. IGUs are common in window replacements and storefront systems where energy performance and condensation control matter.

 Does Master Glass Solutions handle the glass specification? +
 Yes. When you request a quote, we identify the appropriate glass type, thickness, and edge finish for the opening. For code-required locations like showers and doors, we confirm the safety-glass requirement before ordering. Call 210-370-3700 with the opening details, or use the quote form.

 storm-damage-glass.html

 Source: https://www.mgsusa.llc/storm-damage-glass

 STORM & HAIL DAMAGE GLASS REPAIR

 ## Storm-damaged glass gets replaced, fast.

 Hail, wind, falling branches, and flying debris are the most common causes of broken or cracked glass in the San Antonio and Hill Country area. Master Glass Solutions responds to storm-damaged glass across the service area with emergency board-up, insurance-claim documentation, and replacement glass — on buildings only, not vehicles.

 For broken glass in a home or building affecting safety, security, or weather protection, call 210-370-3700 immediately.

 WHEN TO CALL

 ## When to call for storm damage.

 - Hail has cracked, pitted, or shattered window, storefront, or shower glass.
 - Wind or a fallen branch has broken a pane, door glass, or sidelite.
 - Flying debris from a storm has damaged a glass opening.
 - A window or storefront that was fine before a storm now shows a crack, chip, or seal failure.
 - You need documentation and an invoice for an insurance claim on storm-damaged glass.

 HOW IT WORKS

 ## How storm damage glass repair works.

 - 01
 ### Call or submit the details

 Tell us the property address, the damaged opening, the type of storm damage, and whether the situation is urgent. For safety or weather-exposure issues, call 210-370-3700 directly.

 - 02
 ### Secure the opening

 If the glass is broken or at risk of failure, the crew either replaces it or boards up the opening to protect the building until replacement glass is ready.

 - 03
 ### Document and replace

 We document the damage for your insurance claim, confirm the correct glass type and size, and install the replacement. Same-day response is typical for San Antonio metro properties.

 INSURANCE AND COST

 ## Insurance and cost.

 Storm-damaged glass replacement is often covered by homeowner's or commercial property insurance.

 Master Glass Solutions works with most major homeowner's insurance carriers for storm and damage-related glass replacement. We provide a detailed invoice, photos of the damage, and the glass specification for your claim. If you are not sure whether your policy covers the damage, call 210-370-3700 and we will help you understand the next step. Emergency board-up is a separate, typically lower-cost line item — it secures the opening while the replacement glass is cut and scheduled.

 FAQ

 ## Storm damage glass repair questions, answered directly.

 Does homeowner's insurance cover storm-damaged glass? +
 In most cases, yes — hail damage, wind damage, and impact damage from storm debris are covered by standard homeowner's insurance when the damage is to the building's glass. Master Glass Solutions provides a detailed invoice, damage photos, and the glass specification to support your claim. We work with most major homeowner's insurance carriers. Call 210-370-3700 and we will help you understand your coverage.

 What should I do immediately after storm damage to glass? +
 Call 210-370-3700. If the glass is broken, keep people away from the opening until the crew arrives. If weather or security is a concern, the crew will board up the opening the same day. For cracks that have not yet failed, we still recommend a prompt inspection — a crack can spread and a pane can fail without warning after impact.

 How fast can you respond to a storm-damage call? +
 For properties in the San Antonio metro area, we typically respond within about an hour of the call during and after storm events. Response times for outlying Hill Country communities may be longer depending on road conditions and distance. Call 210-370-3700 for an estimated response time to your location.

 Do you handle the insurance paperwork? +
 We provide the documentation your insurance company needs — a detailed invoice, photos of the damage, and the glass specification. The claim itself is between you and your carrier, but Master Glass Solutions makes the documentation part straightforward. If you have a claim number, share it when you call or submit the quote form.

 Is emergency board-up covered by insurance? +
 Emergency board-up is often covered as a mitigation expense under homeowner's and commercial property policies — the idea being that securing the opening prevents additional damage. We invoice board-up separately so you can submit it as part of your claim. Call 210-370-3700 to discuss the situation and get a board-up arranged the same day.

 Do you work on vehicles or windshields after a storm? +
 No. Master Glass Solutions is a building glass contractor. We do not service auto glass, windshields, or any vehicle glass. Storm damage to a vehicle windshield should go to an auto glass shop. Master Glass Solutions handles broken glass in homes and buildings only.

 COMMERCIAL GLASS GUIDE

 ## Commercial glass that fits the building and the business.

 Commercial glass is not a single product — it is a set of choices that affect how a building looks, how customers move through it, how secure it feels, and how much energy it uses. Master Glass Solutions works with storefront systems, entry doors, interior partitions, architectural glazing, and healthcare glazing across San Antonio and Boerne.

 The right commercial glass starts with the opening and the use case. A storefront needs to be clean, visible, and durable. An entry door needs to be barrier-free and secure. An interior partition needs to be the right sightline and operate smoothly day to day. A patient-room door in a clinic needs to be wide, low-threshold, and reliable. Master Glass Solutions matches the glass and hardware to the building, not the other way around.

 WHEN TO START HERE

 ## When to start here.

 - You are planning a new storefront, entry door, or interior glazing for a retail, office, or commercial space.
 - A storefront pane, door, sidelite, or partition needs replacement or repair.
 - You need ADA-compliant openings — barrier-free entry doors, wide patient-room sliding doors, low-threshold access.
 - You are evaluating tempered vs. laminated glass for a commercial opening.
 - You want an estimate that accounts for the opening, the glass type, the hardware, and the schedule.

 HOW IT WORKS

 ## How it works.

 - 01
 ### Share the property and the opening

 Tell us the property address, the type of opening (storefront, door, partition, overhead), the glass and hardware requirements you know about, and any code or ADA considerations.

 - 02
 ### Get the specification right

 We confirm the glass type, thickness, and hardware that fit the opening and the use case — tempered for safety, laminated for security, insulating glass for energy, the right hardware for traffic and ADA.

 - 03
 ### Schedule and install

 For occupied businesses, we schedule around your hours and access constraints. The crew installs the glass and hardware, and cleans up when the work is done.

 WHAT INFLUENCES COMMERCIAL GLASS COST?

 ## What influences commercial glass cost?

 Commercial glass cost is shaped by the opening, the glass specification, the hardware, the framing condition, and the schedule.

 A single storefront pane in an existing frame costs less than a full storefront system with new doors, sidelites, and hardware. A barrier-free patient-room sliding door with fixed sidelites costs more than a standard interior partition because of the width, the hardware, and the ADA requirements. Site access, after-hours scheduling, and any urgent securing needs also affect the quote. A photo, rough dimensions, and a description of the opening are enough to start.

 FAQ

 ## Commercial glass guide questions, answered directly.

 What types of commercial glass do you install? +
 Master Glass Solutions installs storefront glass systems, entry doors, interior partitions, architectural glazing, and healthcare glazing such as patient-room sliding doors. Glass options include tempered, laminated, insulated, and low-E-coated glass. All commercial work meets applicable building-code and safety requirements.

 Do you handle ADA-compliant glass openings? +
 Yes. ADA considerations affect entry doors, patient-room doors, and some interior partitions — things like clear width, threshold height, hardware operation, and swing. Master Glass Solutions installs commercial glass openings that meet ADA requirements, including sliding glass door systems with fixed sidelites for patient rooms in medical facilities.

 How long does a commercial glass installation take? +
 It depends on the scope. A single storefront pane or door glass replacement may be completed in a single visit. A new storefront system with doors, sidelites, and hardware takes longer and is scheduled around your business hours. For multi-opening or architectural work, we provide a timeline with the estimate. Call 210-370-3700 with the project details for a schedule estimate.

 Can you replace glass in an existing storefront frame? +
 Yes. In many cases we can replace the glass in an existing storefront frame without replacing the whole system — this is common after storm damage, break-ins, or when a pane has failed. We measure the opening, match the glass type and size, and install it in the existing frame. If the framing itself is damaged or the system is beyond repair, we discuss a full replacement.

 Do you work with commercial property managers and facility teams? +
 Yes. Master Glass Solutions works with property managers, facility teams, and business owners across San Antonio and Boerne. For occupied buildings, we coordinate scheduling around access constraints and operating hours. For multi-site properties, we can scope each opening individually. Call 210-370-3700 or use the commercial quote form.

 Is tempered or laminated glass better for storefronts? +
 Tempered glass is the standard for storefronts because of its strength and safety properties. Laminated glass adds a plastic interlayer that holds the glass together when broken — useful where security or glass retention matters. Some storefront systems use laminated glass for the door and tempered glass for the sidelites and display panels. We match the specification to the opening and the risk profile.

 GLASS CLEANING & MAINTENANCE GUIDE

 ## Glass that looks good stays looking good with the right care.

 Glass is durable, but water spots, soap scum, hard water stains, and everyday wear add up — especially in a hard-water area like the Texas Hill Country. Master Glass Solutions installs shower enclosures, storefronts, windows, and custom glass across Boerne and San Antonio, and the care routine is part of what keeps that glass performing for years.

 The best glass-cleaning routine is a short, regular one. A squeegee after each shower keeps soap scum and hard water from setting in. For deeper cleaning, a vinegar-and-water mix or a non-abrasive glass cleaner does the job without damaging the glass or the hardware finish. Avoid abrasive scrubbers and harsh chemicals — they can etch the glass and wear the hardware. For storefronts and commercial glass, a clean, lint-free cloth and a standard glass cleaner are usually enough for daily maintenance.

 WHEN TO START HERE

 ## When to start here.

 - Your shower glass has soap scum, hard water spots, or a cloudy film that a regular wipe-down will not remove.
 - You want to keep newly installed glass looking clean without damaging it.
 - Your storefront or window glass has streaks, spots, or buildup that needs a proper clean.
 - You are trying to figure out whether cloudy glass is dirt, hard water, or permanent etching.
 - You want to know what products and tools are safe for tempered, laminated, and coated glass.

 HOW THE ROUTINE WORKS

 ## How the routine works.

 - 01
 ### Daily or after each use — squeegee

 For shower glass, a quick squeegee after each use prevents soap scum and mineral buildup from adhering. It takes seconds and is the single biggest factor in how long glass stays clean.

 - 02
 ### Weekly — gentle wash

 Wash with a mixture of warm water and a few drops of dish soap or a non-abrasive glass cleaner. Use a soft cloth or non-abrasive sponge. Rinse and dry with a lint-free cloth to avoid streaks.

 - 03
 ### For hard water stains — vinegar solution

 A mixture of white vinegar and water (about 1:1) applied with a soft cloth, left to sit briefly, then rinsed and dried, removes most hard water deposits. Repeat as needed for heavier buildup. Avoid vinegar on natural stone surrounds — it can etch stone.

 - 04
 ### What to avoid

 Do not use abrasive scrubbers, steel wool, or harsh acidic or alkaline cleaners on glass. Do not use razor blades on coated or tinted glass unless you know the coating can take it. Avoid cleaners that leave a film — they attract more buildup over time.

 WHEN CLEANING IS NOT ENOUGH

 ## When cleaning is not enough.

 Cloudy, crazed, or permanently etched glass is a replacement problem, not a cleaning problem.

 Hard water stains and soap scum come off with the right cleaning. Permanent etching, crazing, and seal failure on insulated glass units do not — they require replacement. If glass that used to clean up no longer does, or if you see a foggy look between the panes of a double-pane window, call 210-370-3700 and we will tell you whether the glass can be cleaned or needs replacement.

 FAQ

 ## Glass cleaning and maintenance questions, answered directly.

 How do I clean a frameless shower enclosure? +
 Squeegee after each use to prevent soap scum and hard water buildup. For a deeper clean, use a mixture of warm water and a few drops of dish soap or a non-abrasive glass cleaner. Apply with a soft cloth or non-abrasive sponge, rinse, and dry with a lint-free cloth. For hard water stains, a 1:1 white vinegar and water solution applied with a soft cloth, left to sit briefly, then rinsed and dried, removes most deposits. Avoid abrasive scrubbers and harsh chemicals — they can damage the glass and the hardware finish.

 What removes hard water stains from glass? +
 A 1:1 mixture of white vinegar and water applied with a soft cloth, left to sit for a few minutes, then rinsed and dried, removes most hard water stains. For heavier buildup, repeat the process or let the solution sit longer. For glass with a protective coating, check the manufacturer's cleaning recommendations first — some coatings do not tolerate vinegar. Avoid vinegar on natural stone surrounds such as marble or travertine.

 Can I use a razor blade to clean glass? +
 A fresh razor blade held at a shallow angle can remove stubborn deposits from bare, uncoated glass — but it is not safe on coated, tinted, or laminated glass unless you know the coating can take it. For most residential cleaning, a non-abrasive sponge and the right cleaner do the job without the risk. If in doubt, skip the blade and use a dedicated glass-cleaning product.

 Why does my shower glass go cloudy so fast? +
 Soap scum and hard water minerals build up quickly on glass in areas with hard water — and much of the Texas Hill Country has hard water. A squeegee after each use is the single biggest factor in how long glass stays clean. Without it, the buildup bonds to the glass and becomes harder to remove over time. Once the buildup has etched into the surface, it may not come off with cleaning alone — at that point replacement is the right answer.

 How do I clean storefront glass without streaks? +
 Use a clean, lint-free cloth or microfiber towel and a standard glass cleaner or a water-and-dish-soap mixture. Clean from top to bottom in overlapping strokes. Dry with a second clean lint-free cloth to avoid streaks. Clean in shade or during cooler parts of the day — direct sun dries the cleaner too fast and causes streaks. For large storefronts, a squeegee followed by a dry cloth works well.

 When should I replace glass instead of cleaning it? +
 Replace glass when it is permanently etched, crazed, or scratched to the point that cleaning no longer improves it. Replace double-pane windows when the seal has failed and you see fogging or condensation between the panes — the insulating gas is gone and the seal cannot be repaired in the field. Replace glass that is cracked, chipped, or has failed — safety and security come first. Call 210-370-3700 with a description or a photo and we will tell you whether the glass can be cleaned or needs replacement.

 HILL COUNTRY GLASS

 ## Glass that works with Hill Country homes, not against them.

 Hill Country homes are built differently from suburban box construction. Limestone and concrete walls, wide roof spans, deep overhangs, and large openings that bring the outdoors in all create specific glass needs. Master Glass Solutions works with custom glass for Hill Country homes across Boerne, Comfort, Canyon Lake, Wimberley, Blanco, and the surrounding communities — starting with the property and the architecture, not a standard catalog.

 Hill Country construction creates openings that standard residential glass does not always fit well. Thick limestone or concrete walls mean the glass opening is set deep and may need a custom reveal or frame. Wide openings for views and light need glass that is strong enough to span the opening safely. Thermal movement — the difference between a hot Texas afternoon and a cool Hill Country night — matters for large panes and framing choices. Master Glass Solutions measures the actual opening and fabricates glass to fit, rather than forcing a standard size into a non-standard space.

 WHEN TO START HERE

 ## When to start here.

 - You are building or renovating a Hill Country home and need custom glass for an opening that standard sizes do not fit.
 - Your home has limestone, concrete, or thick-wall construction and the glass opening is set deep or non-standard.
 - You want wide-view glass openings that bring in light and landscape without compromising strength or safety.
 - You are choosing between frameless, semi-frameless, and framed glass for a Hill Country interior or exterior opening.
 - You need glass that works with the thermal and weather profile of the Hill Country — heat gain, thermal movement, and storm exposure.

 HOW IT WORKS

 ## How it works.

 - 01
 ### Share the property and the opening

 Tell us the location, the opening type, the construction material around the opening, the view or light you want to achieve, and any thermal or weather considerations you know about.

 - 02
 ### Match the glass to the architecture

 We match the glass type, thickness, and edge finish to the opening and the construction — tempered for safety, thicker stock for wide spans, the right edge detail for the frame or the masonry.

 - 03
 ### Fabricate and install

 We fabricate the glass to the actual opening and install it on site. For Hill Country homes, that often means working around limestone, concrete, or custom framing — we measure first and fit second.

 WHAT INFLUENCES THE INVESTMENT?

 ## What influences the investment?

 Hill Country custom glass cost is shaped by the opening, the glass thickness, the edge work, the framing or reveal, and the site access.

 A standard residential window replacement costs less than a custom wide-view glass opening in a limestone wall. Thick-stock tempered glass for a large span costs more than standard stock because of the material and the fabrication. Custom edge finishes — beveled, polished, or seamed — add a modest premium. Site access in Hill Country communities, seasonal scheduling, and any urgent securing needs also affect the quote. A photo, the opening location, and rough dimensions are enough to start.

 FAQ

 ## Hill Country glass questions, answered directly.

 Why is glass different for Hill Country homes? +
 Hill Country homes are often built with limestone or concrete walls, deep roof spans, and wide openings for views and light. Those construction choices create openings that standard residential glass does not always fit — the opening may be set deep in masonry, the span may be wider than standard stock, or the thermal profile may call for a specific glass type. Master Glass Solutions measures the actual opening and fabricates glass to fit, rather than forcing a standard size into a non-standard space.

 What glass works best for wide-view openings in Hill Country? +
 Tempered glass in 3/8-inch or thicker stock is standard for wide-view openings because of the strength needed to span the opening safely. For very large spans, thicker stock or laminated glass may be appropriate — laminated glass holds together if broken. The right choice depends on the opening size, the framing or reveal, and the load the glass has to carry. Call 210-370-3700 with the opening details and we will match the glass type and thickness to the opening.

 How does limestone construction affect glass installation? +
 Limestone walls set glass openings deep into the masonry, which can mean a custom reveal, a deeper frame, or a glass pocket that standard stock does not fit. The opening may also be non-rectangular — out-of-square, tapered, or with a non-standard reveal depth. Master Glass Solutions measures the actual opening, including the reveal depth and any irregularities, and fabricates or sources glass to fit. A photo of the opening and the surrounding wall helps a lot.

 Do you work with custom home builders and architects in the Hill Country? +
 Yes. Master Glass Solutions works with custom home builders, architects, and homeowners across Boerne, Comfort, Canyon Lake, Wimberley, Blanco, and surrounding communities. For new construction and renovation, we coordinate with the builder and the architect on the glass specification, the schedule, and the installation sequence. Call 210-370-3700 or use the quote form with the project details.

 What about thermal movement in large Hill Country glass openings? +
 Large glass panes in a Hill Country climate experience thermal movement — the glass and the framing expand and contract as the temperature swings from a hot afternoon to a cool night. Framing and installation details account for that movement so the glass is not stressed or bound. For large spans, thicker tempered or laminated glass and the right framing choice matter. We specify the glass and the installation details for the opening, not just the glass alone.

 Can you replace glass in an existing Hill Country home? +
 Yes. We replace glass in existing Hill Country homes for window openings, custom details, shower enclosures, storefronts, and emergency repairs. The same measurement-first approach applies — we measure the actual opening, including any irregularities from the masonry or the framing, and fit the replacement glass to it. Call 210-370-3700 with the property location and the opening details.
